record.paper_title: A Few Problems on Monodromy and Discriminants
record.original_question: Let f:(C^n,0)->(C,0) be an isolated holomorphic function singularity with Milnor number μ, let F(x,λ) be its miniversal deformation over C^μ, and let Σ be the complete bifurcation set of parameters for which f_λ has fewer than μ distinct critical values near the origin. The Lyashko-Looijenga map sends λ to the unordered collection of μ critical values. For a non-simple singularity, what are explicit braid-group obstructions to lifting braids in the configuration space of μ critical values to paths in C^μ minus Σ; equivalently, which braids cannot be lifted?

Let f : (Cn, 0) → (C1, 0) be an isolated holo-
morphic function singularity, µ its Milnor number, F (x, λ) : ( Cn ×
Cµ, 0) → (C1, 0) the miniversal deformation of f , and Σ ⊂ Cµ the
complete bifurcation set of functions of this deformation

The Lyashko–Looijenga map sends any point λ from
a small neighborhood Bε of the origin in Cµ to the unordered collection
of critical values of the function fλ at points close to 0 ∈ Cn

Problem 1A: to present explicit obstructions to the Lyashko-Looijenga
covering in the terms of braid groups. Which braids cannot be lifted to
the space Cµ \ Σ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f:(ℂⁿ,0)→(ℂ,0) be an isolated holomorphic function singularity with Milnor number μ, and let F:(ℂⁿ×ℂ^μ,0)→(ℂ,0), F(x,λ), be a miniversal deformation of f, with f_λ(x):=F(x,λ). Let Σ⊂ℂ^μ denote the complete bifurcation set, i.e. the closed subset consisting of those parameters λ near 0 for which f_λ has strictly fewer than μ distinct Morse critical values in a small fixed neighborhood of 0∈ℂⁿ. On a sufficiently small ball B_ε⊂ℂ^μ around the origin, the Lyashko–Looijenga map LL:B_ε→Sym^μ(ℂ) sends λ to the unordered μ-tuple of critical values of f_λ at the critical points near 0. Restricted to B_ε∖Σ, this map lands in the configuration space Conf_μ(ℂ)=Sym^μ(ℂ)∖{discriminant}, whose fundamental group is the Artin braid group Br_μ.

Assume f is not a simple (ADE) singularity. Provide an explicit description, in terms of the braid group Br_μ, of the obstructions to lifting loops/paths from Conf_μ(ℂ) to B_ε∖Σ via LL. Equivalently, characterize the set of braids β∈Br_μ that cannot be realized as LL∘γ for any path γ in B_ε∖Σ.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as Problem 1A in Vassiliev's 2015 list of problems on monodromy and discriminants (Arnold Math. Journal). Searches turn up only partial observations (e.g. that for any non-simple singularity certain pairwise collisions of critical values along suitable paths are unliftable because two vanishing cycles have intersection number ±2), but no general explicit braid-group description of all obstructions for non-simple singularities has been published. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A Few Problems on Monodromy and Discriminants
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 1A: to present explicit obstructions to the Lyashko-Looijenga covering in the terms of braid groups. Which braids cannot be lifted to the space C^μ \ Σ?
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly stated as an open problem in Vassiliev's problem list.

status_evidence.title: Lyashko-Looijenga morphisms and submaximal factorisations of a Coxeter element
status_evidence.snippet: Treats Lyashko-Looijenga morphisms in the simple/Coxeter setting, where the map is a covering and lifting is unobstructed.
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature handles the simple case where no such braid obstructions arise, leaving the non-simple case open.
